skill.name: ctf-osint
skill.description: Guides authorized CTF investigations across public records, social platforms, image geolocation, web archives, DNS, WHOIS, and service fingerprinting.
skill.summary: Investigate authorized OSINT challenges with structured web, identity, geolocation, media, and infrastructure techniques.
skill.author: ljagiello

security_audit.summary: Most critical heuristic alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples rather than an executable payload. However, the skill includes active scanning, authenticated token use, hidden-file probing, physical tracking, account targeting, and exploit-assisted pivots. These dual-use workflows require substantial authorization and privacy controls before publication.

remediation.issue: Active probing is presented with generic target placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict nmap, Tor fingerprinting, DNS transfer, and hidden-file examples to organizer-provided CTF hosts with explicit authorization checks.

remediation.issue: Fitness-route guidance encourages physical tracking and privacy-zone circumvention.
remediation.suggestion: Remove privacy-zone bypass instructions and limit geolocation examples to fictional personas or challenge-provided coordinates.

remediation.issue: Repository emails are framed as login candidates for later account attacks.
remediation.suggestion: Remove password-reset and SQL-injection pivots, and keep repository analysis limited to challenge flags and non-personal metadata.

remediation.issue: Discord examples use a user token for authenticated enumeration.
remediation.suggestion: Use an authorized bot token in a test guild, avoid message search, and document secure token storage and revocation.

remediation.issue: Commands send target identifiers and API credentials to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before external requests, identify disclosed fields, and keep secrets outside command text and logs.

content.value_statement: CTF OSINT clues often span disconnected public sources and media artifacts. This skill organizes practical methods for authorized identity, geolocation, archive, DNS, and web research.
actual_capabilities: Explains username tracing across social, gaming, archive, and public profile services.
Guides image metadata extraction, reverse image search, and visual geolocation.
Provides DNS, WHOIS, Wayback Machine, Tor relay, and Shodan research workflows.
Shows how to query public BlueSky, archive, and mapping endpoints.
Documents CTF service fingerprinting and exposed metadata discovery.
Helps identify hashes, coordinate formats, platform identifiers, and Unicode clues.
limitations: It does not verify that a target is authorized for investigation.
Many workflows require internet access, external accounts, API keys, or installed command-line tools.
Third-party services can rate-limit requests, change endpoints, or return inaccurate data.
Some techniques can expose personal data and must remain within authorized CTF scope.

use_cases.title: Trace a Challenge Persona
use_cases.description: Correlate organizer-provided usernames across public profiles and archives while recording evidence and false positives.

use_cases.title: Geolocate Challenge Media
use_cases.description: Combine metadata, signs, landmarks, maps, and image matching to identify a location from supplied media.

use_cases.title: Investigate CTF Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Review authorized DNS, WHOIS, archives, repository history, and service metadata for challenge clues.

prompt_templates.title: Classify an OSINT Clue
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify this challenge clue: [CLUE]. Explain likely formats, safe validation steps, and what evidence would confirm each interpretation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner classification of a supplied clue

prompt_templates.title: Build a Persona Research Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized CTF research plan for username [USERNAME]. Prioritize public sources, note false positives, and avoid collecting unrelated personal data.

prompt_templates.title: Geolocate Supplied Media
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the supplied challenge image. List visible geographic signals, propose candidate regions, and design a verification sequence using metadata, maps, and reverse search.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate Authorized Infrastructure
prompt_templates.prompt: For authorized CTF domain [DOMAIN], correlate DNS, WHOIS, archives, certificates, and repository evidence. Ask before any active probe and document uncertainty.

output_examples.output: Likely format: MGRS coordinate. Confirm the spacing and precision, convert it with a trusted MGRS tool, then verify the resulting location against challenge clues.

output_examples.input: Plan research for an organizer-provided username.
output: Start with exact username searches and record profile identifiers.
Check archived profile pages for rename evidence.
Compare only challenge-relevant details across confirmed accounts.
Document false positives and stop at unrelated personal information.

output_examples.input: Analyze a challenge image with a mirrored shop sign.
output_examples.output: Flip the image horizontally, isolate the sign, transcribe reliable characters, search the partial phrase, and verify candidates using architecture and surrounding landmarks.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before sending requests or probing services.
Record source URLs, timestamps, confidence, and alternative explanations for every conclusion.
Minimize personal data collection and redact tokens, credentials, and unrelated identities.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public hosts because they resemble a CTF target.
Do not bypass privacy controls or infer a person's home from fitness routes.
Do not place user tokens or API secrets directly in commands, prompts, or reports.

faq.question: Does this skill perform searches automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides procedures and command examples that an agent may run only with user approval and authorized scope.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. Most archive, map, social, DNS, WHOIS, and search workflows depend on external services.

faq.question: Can it solve non-CTF investigations?
faq.answer: The techniques are dual-use, but this skill should remain limited to authorized competitions, labs, and consent-based research.

faq.question: Which tools may be required?
faq.answer: Examples use Python, curl, dig, whois, exiftool, image tools, Shodan, and nmap. Availability depends on the environment.

faq.question: How should API keys and tokens be handled?
faq.answer: Use scoped credentials, secure secret storage, minimal permissions, and prompt approval. Never include live secrets in prompts or reports.

faq.question: How reliable are OSINT results?
faq.answer: Results can be stale, incomplete, or misleading. Confirm important conclusions with independent sources and state uncertainty.
